title: GOOD: to_ipv4_mapped() not to_ipv4() for IPv4 normalization
description: In session.rs the IPv6-to-IPv4 normalization uses Ipv6Addr::to_ipv4_mapped() rather than to_ipv4(). The distinction matters: to_ipv4() also converts deprecated IPv4-compatible addresses (::x.x.x.x, i.e. the 96-bit all-zero prefix) to IPv4, whereas to_ipv4_mapped() converts only the RFC 4291 §2.5.5.2 IPv4-mapped form (::ffff:x.x.x.x). IPv4-compatible addresses are deprecated in RFC 4291 and must not be silently promoted to IPv4 for CIDR matching — doing so would cause a whitelisted 192.168.0.0/16 block to incorrectly match the deprecated ::192.168.1.50 form in addition to the intended ::ffff:192.168.1.50 form. The code comments this choice explicitly, naming the RFC and the alternative avoided. Alternative rejected: to_ipv4(), which is the more commonly reached-for method but is subtly incorrect for this use case because it matches a second address class that should be left as native IPv6.
